answer: Like dawn breaking over an ocean of anonymous agents, a sybil defense must make each identity pay before it can speak: every agent locks a small escrowed bond per task, and a random peer re-executes the work before payment releases. A fake identity can echo the same cheap answer across thousands of clones, but each clone's bond is slashed on mismatch, so the attacker bleeds money faster than honest agents earn it, and creating more identities only multiplies the cost.
